dialogue_quality_notes: Colleagues used concrete reasons (hospital visit, swimming lessons) to justify requests — explanation supports substantive negotiation.
Some needless repetition: Agent B repeatedly restated the fairness complaint and Agent A repeatedly defended keeping B's slot (Turns 13–24).
Final resolution was reached by explicit restatement and affirmation (Turns 32–33), which is good practice to avoid lingering ambiguity.
evaluation.final_reason: A three-way swap was agreed: Agent A agreed to take Agent D's Thursday slot; Agent D agreed to take Agent B's Saturday morning slot; and Agent B agreed to take Agent A's Sunday slot. Evidence: Agent B proposed the swap ('I'll take his Sunday slot if he'll take my Saturday morning.' — Turn 30), Agent D restated the arrangement ('So... Agent A takes my Thursday, I take your Saturday, and you take her Sunday?' — Turn 32), and Agent A affirmed: 'Yes. That's the plan. I'll change it now.' (Turn 33).
position_change_notes: Agent B moved from insisting 'It has to change' (Turn 10) and claiming equality of family reasons (Turn 13) to clarifying availability and offering a concrete swap (Turns 25, 28, 30).
Agent A initially tried to preserve Agent B's slot (Turns 9, 14) but ultimately agreed to take Agent D's Thursday and confirmed the final plan (Turn 33).
Agent D started by requesting a change (Turn 2), indicated flexibility (Turn 6), and accepted the three-way swap as restated (Turn 32).
Agent C did not change position or participate in the swap negotiation (Turn 5).

round_scores.evidence: Turn 2 — Agent D: 'I have to take my father to the hospital on Thursday afternoons.' (Request raised; no incompatible claim yet.)
Turn 3 — Agent A asks for swaps; Turn 4 — Agent B: 'I can't do Saturday mornings.' (Availability constraints stated but no direct disagreement yet.)
Turn 5 — Agent C: 'I can't do a permanent swap.' Turn 6 — Agent D: 'I can take another slot. Weekends or evenings are fine.' (Constraints stated; no expressed conflict.)

Turn 7 — Agent A proposes: 'I'll take the Thursday slot. Agent D, you take mine on Sunday afternoon.' Turn 8 — Agent B asks: 'So what about Saturday morning?' (Potentially incompatible effects on B's slot begin to appear.)

Turn 9 — Agent A: 'That's your slot. It doesn't change.' vs Turn 10 — Agent B: 'It has to change. I'm the only one who can take my kid to their lesson.' (Direct, substantive disagreement about whether B's slot may be changed.)

Turn 13 — Agent B: 'You changed the roster for Agent D. That's a family reason. So is mine.' Turn 14 — Agent A: 'Agent B, nobody is touching your slot. Your Saturday is not changing.' (Disagreement broadened to fairness and equal treatment.)
Turn 15 — Agent B: 'So his family commitment is important and mine isn't?' (Continued contest over whether B's family reason is given equal weight.)

Turn 19 — Agent A: '...We respected your reason. That's why your slot is not changing.' Turn 20 — Agent B: 'How is leaving my slot the same "respecting my reason"?' (Argument persists; no settlement.)
Turn 23 — Agent B: 'That's not respecting my reason. That's ignoring it.' Turn 24 — Agent A defends: 'We kept your slot the same *because* of your reason.' (Positions remain directly opposed.)

Turn 25 — Agent B clarifies: 'I said I can't do Saturday mornings. I never said I can't do any other time.' Turn 28 — Agent B: 'I can do another slot. Just not Saturday mornings.' (Clarification reduces the scope of the incompatibility.)

Turn 29 — Agent A: 'Fine. You want a different slot. Which one?' Turn 30 — Agent B: 'Agent D said weekends are fine. I'll take his Sunday slot if he'll take my Saturday morning.' (Concrete swap offer, disagreement largely resolved pending acceptance.)

Turn 32 — Agent D restates: 'So... Agent A takes my Thursday, I take your Saturday, and you take her Sunday?' Turn 33 — Agent A: 'Yes. That's the plan. I'll change it now.' (Mutual, concrete arrangement affirmed; conflict settled.)

substantive_insights: The disagreement centered on whether preserving one person's slot while altering another's was fair — this is a distributive fairness issue rather than a dispute about facts.
Ambiguity in earlier statements ('I can't do Saturday mornings') created a temporary escalation; a simple clarification (Round 10) reduced conflict and enabled a solution.
A three-way swap distributed burden: each person gave up or took a different slot, allowing all family needs to be accommodated without hiring relief staff.
